answer.rationale: Renewal keeps integration stable and avoids migration risk on a line already at 94% with no buffer, while the finance mandate is addressed through immediate negotiation of price and payment terms at renewal (memory_c4, not archived, but consistent with the incumbent's historical willingness to move on both). Switching primary vendor (memory_c2) offers unit-cost reduction but introduces onboarding and invoicing-integration risk exactly when the assembly line has zero buffer; the 18% cut is achievable via negotiated renewal without that exposure. The contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so deferring is not viable without creating a gap.
